missing.name: Arena-score nowcasting: simulate the pairwise-vote mechanism that settles the monthly 'best AI model' markets
missing.one_line: Run your own judge-model pairwise battles between a new release and the incumbents, fit Bradley-Terry with the leaderboard's own uncertainty, and price where a low-vote Arena score will converge by the monthly snapshot.
missing.scope: Cover the recurring 'Which company has the best AI model end of <month>?' family. Rules fetched today: the market resolves on the arena.ai Text Arena Overall board with style control OFF, checked at 12:00 ET on the last day of the month. Rank decides, ties go to Arena score, and AutoEval-marked models are excluded. The file needs two layers. (1) Statistics only: turn the published score, CI and vote count into P(rank flip by snapshot) as votes accumulate. New entrants sit near 5k votes at +/-8-9, while incumbents sit at 40-75k votes at +/-3-4. (2) Simulated votes: a cross-family judge panel battles the new model against incumbents on an Arena-like prompt mix. Length and markdown preference must be reproduced, not removed, because the market uses the no-style-control board. The output is a forecast of the converged score before the leaderboard has enough votes. Add release-calendar OSINT, the lab private-testing selection effect, and vote rigging as a manipulation risk on the resolution source. State plainly that whether specialist traders already do this is unverified. Boundaries: enumerable human panels stay in critic-pool-panel-twins. Release-date markets are out of scope.
missing.why_it_matters: This is the one place where an LLM simulation has a validated correlation above 0.9 with the exact statistic that settles a liquid, recurring market. Arena-Hard-Auto reports 98.6% correlation with Arena human-preference rankings for about $20 a run [pre-2025, possibly stale]. Length-controlled AlpacaEval reaches Spearman 0.98 [pre-2025, possibly stale]. The September 2026 event has $3.63M volume and $1.45M liquidity, with Anthropic at 0.9855. The October event already shows $352k volume and $679k liquidity across 21 company markets. Live board, updated 2026-09-13: #1 is at 1508 +/-8 on 5,783 votes, and a Google entrant is at 1495 +/-9 on 5,076 votes. The race sits inside the CI, so the edge is the convergence forecast. Twelve or more resolutions a year give statistical power that the list's one-off events lack. Cheap validation: run a retro on the last 10-15 frontier releases, comparing a judge-BT prediction from release-day API access against the score at 30k votes. Then log daily board snapshots against prices for three monthly cycles.
missing.flags: Never submit Arena votes on a market you hold. Vote rigging with a few hundred votes is documented and would be manipulation of the resolution source. Lab staff hold MNPI on releases and private Arena tests. Judge self-preference bias needs a cross-family panel. Tech category taker feeRate is 0.04, so prefer maker expression. The top rank is structurally fragile: one paper reports 92% top-1 swaps on held-out splits.

missing.name: Outside-view engine: procedural-clock feasibility and reference-class hazards for 'by date' ladders
missing.one_line: Compile each 'will X happen by date' market into the formal procedure that must complete, attach computed reference-class completion-time distributions, and sell rungs that are procedurally infeasible or priced above the outside-view hazard.
missing.scope: (a) Procedure-graph extraction: steps, minimum durations and veto points for legislative calendars, treaty ratification, court scheduling, launch licensing, merger reviews and UNSC procedure. (b) Reference-class tournament: three or more candidate classes with computed base rates, not remembered ones, a red-team challenge on class membership, and a Fermi cross-check. This section should absorb the two duplicate reference-class variants now sitting in adversarial-debate-price-residual and sponsor-and-inform-niche-models. (c) Hazard term structure across the ladder: fit a constant or Weibull hazard and compare it with the market-implied one. Calendar spreads, rung k minus rung k-1, isolate 'happens in month k'. (d) Deadline-effect correction for bargaining events: agreements cluster right before the deadline, so the hazard is back-loaded, not constant. Present the negatives. Prompt-only base-rate tricks add little, so the edge has to come from the data pipeline. Insider flow dominates late in geopolitics ladders. 'Nothing ever happens' NO-buying already exists as a 987-star meme bot with no published PnL. Capital locks for months. Validation: on 60+ resolved by-date ladders after model cutoffs, compare market-implied and realised hazard by category and time-to-deadline. Then test whether 'minimum remaining procedural steps' improves log-loss over price alone. Score event-clustered.
missing.why_it_matters: By-date ladders are among the most liquid non-sports books. The US-Iran final nuclear deal ladder has $17.84M volume, $404k liquidity and 8 rungs. The US-Russia nuclear deal ladder has $662k volume. The list handles these ladders only inside the geopolitics wargame entry, using simulation, the most biased tool in the band. The outside view is the best-documented human debiasing method. Mechanism: completion-time optimism, plus acquiescence. In Buehler 1994 only 13% finished by their own 50% date and 45% by their 99% date. Geopolitics is fee-free, so small hazard edges are tradable. The engine is also the natural home for the list's orphaned reference-class material.
missing.flags: Geopolitics markets face insider-trading scrutiny. War-related contracts are restricted in some jurisdictions. NO positions on long ladders lock capital for months. This overlaps the behavioural-bias band if that band already has a 'YES-optimism / status-quo' entry, so check for duplication.

missing.name: Reward-pool minority game: simulate where rival farmers will quote tomorrow and sit where they will not
missing.one_line: Treat liquidity-reward allocation as a repeated minority game. A population model of rival makers forecasts next-day dilution per pool, and the LP bot allocates to the best predicted reward per unit of jump risk.

Model: a heterogeneous farmer population of rate-chasers, competitiveness-chasers, category specialists and sponsored-pool sprinters. Crowd-anticrowd dynamics predict overshoot, so pools that looked empty yesterday are crowded today. Combine this with a jump-risk score built from scheduled catalysts and category gap and dispute rates, so that 'uncontested' does not mean 'gap-risk dump'. Evidence from the E2 pack, not re-fetched: 16,719 pools configured at $585k a day against $108-156k a day actually paid. Rate divided by competitiveness spans seven orders of magnitude. 23.5% of configured rate sits in competitiveness-0 markets. The top 10 wallets take 24%, and the median payout is about $5. In the Telonex case, makers doubled within a day of a sponsorship. Fetched today: five NFL moneylines with identical $15,771-a-day pools show competitiveness from 1.28 to 8.78. Then A/B the allocator against rate-ranked allocation, net of markout.

missing.name: Active price probing: measure order-book resilience with small real trades and use it as the deference signal
missing.one_line: Spend a few dollars of genuine taker flow to learn whether a price is defended by informed liquidity or is soft and stale, and let the measured resilience set how much weight the stacker gives the market.
missing.scope: Design: randomised small marketable orders of $5-20 in both directions, held and not cancelled. Measure refill time, reversion half-life, and which maker addresses refill, taken from on-chain fills because feed direction is only about 59% accurate (E1 pack). The output is a per-market resilience score. It feeds the act-abstain gate in market-anchored-selective-deference and the LP quote width. Evidence comes from a field experiment with 5-point shocks on 817 markets. 75% of the shock remained after one week and 56% after 60 days. One-week reversion was 47% where an external estimate existed and 23% where it did not. It was 33% against 17% for above- and below-median trader counts, and 49% for above-median volume. Softness is therefore predictable, and soft prices carry the least information. The file must state that the venue was Manifold (play-money Mana, with a Sweepcash follow-up) and that no Polymarket replication exists. Validation: 100 thin markets with a randomised probe against a no-probe control. Test whether resilience predicts the later agent-versus-market Brier gap and the LP markout. The budget is a few hundred dollars of fees and spread.
missing.why_it_matters: This is the only idea in the band where the agent creates information by interacting with the market, not by reading about the event. It answers the list's central question, 'should we disagree with the price here?', with a measurement and not a model. It is cheap, fast, and reuses the owner's execution stack. It also corrects a weakness in the list, which cites the 60-day persistence result as if it described Polymarket.
missing.flags: Probes must be genuine risk-transferring trades. Orders placed with intent to cancel are spoofing. Self-fills breach the ToS clause on 'no change in beneficial ownership', which has no intent element (E9 pack). Never size or time probes to move thin books, trigger news citations or set off others' rules. Get a legal review before systematic use. Taker fees apply.

key_evidence.note: 2025-03, Rasooly and Rozzi, 'How manipulable are prediction markets?': 817 Manifold markets, 5-point shocks. 75% of the shock remains at one week and 56% at 60 days. Resilience rises with external estimates, trader count and volume. Play-money venue.

missing.name: Two-crowd differential: use the Polymarket US versus international price gap as a sentiment index, not an arbitrage
missing.category: Cross-venue signal (route to the cross-venue band if no equivalent exists there)
missing.one_line: Two legally separated crowds price the same events under one brand. Log both books, learn which crowd is better calibrated by category and horizon, and trade only on the venue you can lawfully access.
missing.scope: Grounding: the closed-end-fund discount as a sentiment index (Lee, Shleifer, Thaler 1991) and twin-listed shares. Both venues list public market-data endpoints. Steps: match events across the two books. Adjust for rule differences, because the US book settles by exchange determination with a death carve-out at last traded price, while the international book settles through UMA. Compute per-category calibration of each book on resolved events. The signal is the gap times the learned reliability. This is explicitly not an arbitrage, because one controlled group cannot lawfully hold both legs (E9 pack). Unknowns: the size of the overlap outside sports. My arXiv query for lead-lag between the books returned nothing relevant. Validation: 8 weeks of logging and 300+ matched resolved markets.
missing.why_it_matters: The E1, E5 and E9 packs all stress that the two books are separate populations: KYC'd US retail and intermediaries on one side, global crypto-native traders on the other. The packs give international at $4.59B and US at $3.82B for August 2026. No entry in this band uses the population difference as information. Partisan and home-team composition effects are testable for free.
missing.flags: US persons may not touch the international venue, and entities they control may not either. Polymarket US market data are licensed as 'personal, non-commercial' (E9 pack), so check before systematic collection.

WIDEN critic-pool-panel-twins into 'culture panels: critic, jury and audience twins'. (a) Add Eurovision-class contests, where national juries plus televote are aggregated mechanically. Route reward-pool-minority-game to the incentives or LP band and two-book-crowd-differential to the cross-venue band.

CROSS-BAND NOTE, outside this band, listed so the orchestrator can check it exists elsewhere. Since 2026-08-07 crypto up/down markets settle on a Chainlink TWAP (a 60 s window for 5-minute markets from 2026-08-14), while Kalshi settles on an average of 60 one-second CF Benchmarks prints (E1 and E5 packs). Near expiry the contract is an Asian digital, not a European one. Averaging compresses terminal variance, and the two venues carry an index basis. If no quant-band entry prices the averaging window explicitly, that is a gap. Speculative LLM methods add nothing at this horizon, which is why the band rightly has no short-duration-crypto entry.

COVERAGE NOTE. The band has no sports entry, and that is defensible. The E4 pack finds no favourite-longshot bias in sports, about 1% margins for the winners, and four frontier agents that failed to beat the market on 104 World Cup matches. The only sports-adjacent speculative surface is same-game dependence, which is already inside dependence-pricing-combos-joint. 'Will X beat earnings' markets exist but are too small for a Finance entry: nine live markets at $0.6k-$4.4k volume and $0.2k-$1.5k liquidity (Gamma API, fetched today).
misclassified: sponsor-and-inform-niche-models: the sub-variant 'Options-implied density vs BTC threshold ladders' is an established cross-venue quant trade. The E5 pack measures a 5.6-point gap with a roughly 4-hour half-life, which may be a premium. It is not speculative and has nothing to do with sponsoring liquidity. Move it to the cross-venue or quant band.

evaluation-promotion-allocation-metalayer: it is filed as a Speculative-novel strategy but says itself that none of it is alpha, so it fails the band's criterion (a). 'Purely theoretical' is also wrong for most components. Frozen-snapshot replay (Hindcast, OracleProto) and anytime-valid gating exist as published, tested methods, and the changelog watcher is ordinary engineering. Reclassify it as shared infrastructure. Only changelog-reactive re-optimisation is a strategy.

crowd-price-path-simulation: two of its six sub-variants, under-reaction drift and dislocation fade, are statistical trades with hard on-chain evidence. They belong to the behavioural or microstructure band. FACT CHECK: the '817 markets, shocks visible after 60 days' field experiment ran on Manifold, which is play-money Mana with a small Sweepcash follow-up, not on Polymarket (arXiv 2503.03312 HTML, fetched today). The entry presents it as persistence evidence without naming the venue. The same paper shows reversion is much faster in higher-volume markets and where an external estimate exists.

speaker-twin-mention-montecarlo: the 'Emerging' maturity rests on the NO-side laddered maker overlay. That overlay is a structural and behavioural maker strategy (YES overpricing in mention markets), and its only profit record is self-reported. The twin itself has negative evidence: Brier 0.1470 against 0.1402 for the market, and a public live record of -$16.40. Label the twin 'Experimental' and route the NO-ladder to the behavioural-bias or LP band.

rules-ambiguity-hazard-layer: components (c), the dispute-hazard haircut for 95-99c sniping, and (e), the cross-venue spec-diff, are risk controls for the owner's existing sniping and cross-venue suites. The E3 pack shows rule readers already won the Iran ceasefire-extension market, where YES sat at 0.1-0.3c. They are not speculative. Only (a) the scanner, (b) the ambiguity wargame and (d) rule-diff versioning fit this band.

external-forecaster-sourcing: tier 2, Numinous SN6 mining, earns token emissions for predicting the 7-day-later Polymarket price. It is a second revenue line in a volatile token, not Polymarket PnL. Route it to the services or other-revenue band. The seed label 'synthetic crowd / internal prediction market' is a stretch, because it is an external crowd.

market-anchored-selective-deference: the seed_category 'self-improving / recursive forecasting agents' is cosmetic. The entry is an aggregation and gating layer with nothing recursive in it. The day-zero quoting sub-variant is an LP strategy (see the split suggestion).

semantic-market-graph-relative-value: the seed_category 'multi-agent adversarial debate forecasting' is a stretch. The core is structural relative value and lead-lag, with debate used only to pick the wrong leg. Coherent-polytope arbitrage is an established practice that the list itself sizes at about $95k realised. Only the LLM-filtered lead-lag and the precomputed playbooks are speculative.

agent-society-simulation-forecasting: 'Emerging' overstates maturity. The band rule allows 'Emerging' when early real examples exist, but every example cited has no backtest or is negative: the bridge repos show no PnL, the n=5 calibration had rho flip sign, and there are four wargaming failure papers. 'Experimental' is the honest label. The defensible uses the entry itself lists (branch enumeration, ladder hazard coherence, tripwires) overlap with the proposed outside-view engine.

evolutionary-agent-strategy-factory: the sub-variant 'Builder-code monetisation of proven agents' contradicts the E6 pack. The median builder could gross at most about $300 a month at the 100 bps cap. Every fill routed through a builder code is publicly enumerable with maker address and owner id, and codes are revocable for 'automated' or 'self-referred' flow. A proven strategy routed through a labelled code is leaked. Move monetisation to the services band and delete it here.

dependence-pricing-combos-joint: caveats to add. docs.polymarket.com does carry Combos pages, including collateral return in pUSD (llms.txt, fetched today). But the overview page states nothing on venue availability, eligibility or fees, and the E1 pack dates the launch to Polymarket US on 2026-08-21. The E4 pack also reports that Polymarket is building an in-house desk for RFQ parlays, so the RFQ counterparty may be the house as well as Jump-class firms. Both belong in the entry's flags.

simulated-stakeholder-polling / decision-body-member-twins / elite-selection-bargaining-simulators / synthetic-uma-dispute-jury all carry the seed label 'simulated stakeholder polling'. Only the first is polling. The other three are institutional twins. This is harmless for coverage, since the seed has its own entry. The owner should not read it as four takes on one idea, though. Only one of them tests polling simulation.
weakest_entries: evaluation-promotion-allocation-metalayer: by its own text it has no mechanism for beating the price. It is necessary as infrastructure but is not a strategy file. Make it an appendix and keep only changelog-reactive re-optimisation as an entry.

information-partitioned-delphi-panel: it rests on a single paper (Brier 0.216 to 0.178 on 375 questions) that was never benchmarked against the market price. The gain vanishes once evidence is shared. The entry concludes it is 'a disagreement and uncertainty signal for other strategies, not standalone alpha'. Fold it into the synthetic-crowd file.

decision-body-member-twins: tradable capacity is $4.3k volume on FOMC dissents. There are 8 meetings a year against a bar of roughly 350 predictions. FedSight has no futures baseline and no leakage control. Roll-call accuracy is mostly party-line. Aaru concedes Powell-class individuals cannot be simulated. Only the legislative whip-count on pivotal members has capacity plausible enough to justify the work. Merge it into the elite-selection file.

critic-pool-panel-twins, as currently scoped: RT ladders hold $2.7k-$31.6k. The entry admits humans already trade RT statistically, the twin adds nothing after 30-50 reviews, the LLM taste layer has negative evidence (super-omnivorous bias), and individual twins correlate at r=0.20. It earns a file only if widened to the large mechanically aggregated events. Eurovision 2026 shows $193.9M volume, and Oscars and audience-demand brackets add more. Even then, bookmakers anchor Eurovision, and a published voting model did not beat betting tables.

external-forecaster-sourcing: for tier 1, the top public agents only tie the Kalshi baseline (0.8022 against 0.7998), and anyone with real edge trades it directly. Tier 2 is token mining. Tier 3, a staked commit-reveal tournament, is legally heavy and adversely selected for a solo team. What survives is an 8-week ingestion test of one more expert inside the stacker. That is a task, not a file.

sponsor-and-inform-niche-models: the mechanism is real, since the list cites the FluSight ensemble beating disease markets so clearly that the optimal blend puts zero weight on them, against only $20.1k resting liquidity on measles. But the economics are likely negative for a small team. The one documented sponsorship cost about $70k and doubled the competing makers within a day. Farmers dilute the subsidy, other makers copy model-driven quotes, and whether the ToS allows trading a market you lobbied for and sponsored is unverified. Keep it only as a $20-a-day, 14-day experiment on an existing thin market. Drop the 'pitch a new market' branch until the ToS question is answered.

llm-monoculture-herd-factor is borderline. The decisive input, the LLM share of Polymarket volume, is unmeasured, and the '30% of wallets' figure is a vendor claim. The one direct test of fading LLM consensus, on 104 World Cup matches, was unprofitable. It deserves a file only because the validation is pure logging at zero capital. If the 12-week log shows no news-free drift toward the sentinel, delete the file and do not iterate on it.

agent-society-simulation-forecasting is an owner seed and must stay, but the owner should treat it as weak. Every cited validation is absent or negative. The only validated capability of OASIS-class simulators is propagation scale at about 30% NRMSE (E8 pack), which the entry does not use. Expect base-rate shrinkage to do all the work in the blind test. Pre-register 'shrunk sim equals base rate only' as the kill condition.
